subject: Genetics
title: Minimal Genome
description: A micro-lesson that makes Minimal Genome usable.

hook.text: What's the smallest genome that can support life? Venter's team stripped genes one by one to find out.

buildup.text: They created JCVI-syn3.0 with just 473 genes—the smallest genome of any self-replicating organism ever known.

discovery.text: Of those 473 genes, 149 have unknown function. We stripped life to its minimum—and still don't understand a third of it.

twist.text: The minimal cell divided into strange shapes. Adding 76 genes back fixed it.

climax.text: The minimal genome shows how much we don't know. Even the simplest life holds mysteries we haven't decoded.

punchline.text: We built the simplest life. We still can't explain it all.

quiz.question: How many genes does the minimal synthetic genome have?
